name: Impatiens
climate: Temperate to tropical depending on type; frost tender
tip: Protect from hot afternoon sun and drying winds.

name: Salvia
water: Moderate; drought tolerant once established for many species
climate: Temperate to subtropical depending on species
tip: Deadhead or trim after flowering to encourage another flush.

name: Verbena
climate: Temperate to subtropical
tip: Trim lightly when plants become leggy to maintain dense flowering growth.

name: Lobelia
water: Regular; do not allow containers to dry out
climate: Cool-season temperate to subtropical
tip: Use afternoon shade in warm districts to extend flowering.

name: Aster
harvest: Flowers about 14–20 weeks depending on type
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Good airflow helps limit foliar disease; divide perennial clumps periodically.

name: Chrysanthemum
harvest: Flowers typically in autumn; months from cuttings
climate: Temperate to subtropical
tip: Pinch growing tips before flower-bud formation for bushier plants.

name: Gerbera
depth: Seed about 5 mm; crown at soil surface
harvest: Flowers within 4–6 months from established young plants
water: Moderate; keep crown dry and soil well drained
climate: Temperate to subtropical
tip: Never bury the crown deeply because this encourages rot.

name: Carnation
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Pinch young shoots to encourage branching and support tall flowering stems if needed.

name: Dianthus
climate: Cool to temperate; some types suit mild subtropics
tip: Deadhead regularly and provide excellent drainage.

name: Delphinium
harvest: Flowers about 5–7 months or following season
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Tall flower spikes need shelter or staking; all parts are toxic if eaten.

name: Lupin
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Direct sow where possible because lupins form a taproot and dislike disturbance.

name: Phlox
harvest: Flowers about 12–18 weeks depending on type
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Maintain airflow and avoid wet foliage to reduce mildew.

name: Primrose
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Protect from hot afternoon sun and keep roots cool with mulch.

name: Ranunculus
harvest: Flowers about 12–16 weeks after growth starts
water: Regular during active growth; reduce after foliage yellows
climate: Cool-season temperate to subtropical
tip: Plant corms with claw-like points facing downward in well-drained soil.

name: Anemone
climate: Cool-season temperate to subtropical
tip: Soaking dry corms briefly before planting can help establish growth.

name: Gladiolus
climate: Temperate to subtropical
tip: Plant batches a few weeks apart for a longer display and stake tall stems in windy sites.

name: Iris
propagation: Rhizomes or bulbs depending on type
depth: Bearded rhizomes partly exposed; bulbs about 5–10 cm
climate: Cool to temperate; some species suit warmer zones
tip: For bearded iris, avoid burying rhizomes deeply and divide crowded clumps.

name: Tulip
climate: Cool to temperate; bulbs may require chilling in mild-winter areas
tip: Plant bulbs in autumn after adequate chilling where winters are warm.

name: Daffodil
depth: 10–15 cm or about twice bulb height
water: Regular during active growth; drier during dormancy
climate: Cool to temperate; many cultivars suit mild areas
tip: Allow foliage to yellow naturally after flowering so bulbs replenish energy.

name: Hyacinth
climate: Cool to temperate; chilling may help in warm areas
tip: Use gloves if sensitive to bulb sap and ensure free-draining soil.

name: Freesia
climate: Temperate to subtropical cool season
tip: Plant in groups for stronger displays and reduce watering as foliage dies back.

name: Agapanthus
harvest: Summer flowers; divisions may flower within 1–2 seasons
climate: Temperate to subtropical
tip: Check local weed guidance before planting because agapanthus can spread readily in some areas.

name: Bird of Paradise
depth: Plant crown at soil level; seed 1–2 cm
harvest: Flowers after 3–5 years from seed; sooner from mature divisions
water: Regular while establishing; moderate when mature
climate: Warm temperate to tropical; protect from hard frost
tip: Avoid frequent division because established clumps flower best when left relatively undisturbed.

name: Bougainvillea
harvest: Flowers/bracts within 1–2 years from established plants
climate: Warm temperate to tropical; frost sensitive
tip: Avoid overwatering and excessive nitrogen, which promote leaves instead of flowering.

name: Hibiscus
harvest: Flowers within the growing season from established plants
climate: Subtropical to tropical; some types suit warm temperate gardens
tip: Feed during active growth and prune to maintain shape and encourage new flowering wood.

name: Gardenia
climate: Warm temperate to subtropical
tip: Gardenias prefer acidic soil and can develop yellow leaves in alkaline conditions.

name: Hydrangea
harvest: Flowers from established plants each season
climate: Cool to temperate; protected subtropical sites
tip: Protect from harsh afternoon sun; pruning timing depends on whether the cultivar flowers on old or new wood.

name: Jasmine
climate: Temperate to subtropical depending on species
tip: Provide a trellis or support for climbing species and prune after flowering.

name: Camellia
depth: Plant slightly high, never bury trunk base
climate: Cool to temperate and mild subtropical
tip: Use acidic organic mulch and protect roots from hot drying conditions.

name: Azalea
climate: Cool to temperate and mild subtropical
tip: Avoid lime and alkaline soil; mulch to keep shallow roots cool.

name: Rhododendron
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Shelter from hot afternoon sun and drying winds; ensure excellent drainage.

name: Grevillea
depth: Seed about 5 mm; nursery plant at existing level
water: Moderate while establishing; low to moderate once mature
climate: Australian temperate to subtropical depending on species
tip: Use low-phosphorus native fertiliser and avoid waterlogged soil.

name: Bottlebrush
depth: Surface sow fine seed; plants at nursery level
harvest: Flowers within 2–3 years from young plants
water: Regular while establishing; many tolerate periods of dryness once mature
climate: Temperate to subtropical; species vary
tip: Prune lightly after flowering to maintain shape and encourage dense growth.

name: Banksia
water: Low to moderate once established; excellent drainage
climate: Australian temperate to subtropical depending on species
tip: Choose a banksia native to similar soil and rainfall conditions; avoid high-phosphorus fertiliser.

name: Wattle
water: Moderate while establishing; low once mature for many species
climate: Wide Australian range depending on species
tip: Select local or regionally suitable Acacia species because size and climate tolerance vary greatly.

name: Waratah
depth: Seed 5–10 mm; plants at nursery level
climate: Cool to temperate, particularly suitable to southeastern Australian conditions
tip: Keep roots cool and moist but never waterlogged; avoid high-phosphorus fertiliser.

name: Kangaroo Paw
depth: Seed about 3–5 mm; crown at soil level
water: Moderate during active growth; good drainage
climate: Temperate to warm temperate; cultivars vary
tip: Remove old flower stems and damaged leaves at the base to maintain airflow.

name: Flannel Flower
climate: Temperate eastern Australian conditions
tip: Avoid disturbing established roots and use a free-draining sandy mix.

name: Everlasting Daisy
water: Moderate during establishment; lower once growing strongly
climate: Temperate to arid depending on species
tip: Direct sow into open sunny soil and avoid excessive fertiliser.

name: Pigface
depth: Cuttings laid/inserted shallowly; seed surface sown
harvest: Flowers within months; edible fruit follows flowering on suitable species
climate: Coastal, temperate, arid and warm regions depending on species
tip: Excellent drainage is essential; ideal for exposed, sandy and coastal sites.

name: Saltbush
harvest: Leaves can be lightly harvested once plants are well established
water: Low to moderate; drought tolerant once established
climate: Arid, semi-arid and temperate Australian regions depending on species
tip: Regular light tip-pruning encourages tender leafy growth for culinary use.

name: Muntries
water: Moderate while establishing; drought tolerant once mature
climate: Temperate southern Australian conditions
tip: Use as a spreading groundcover or train lightly; protect fruit from birds.

name: Quandong
climate: Arid, semi-arid and dry temperate Australia
tip: Quandong is semi-parasitic and needs suitable host plants nearby for reliable growth.

name: Riberry
depth: Seed about 5–10 mm; plants at nursery level
climate: Subtropical to tropical eastern Australia
tip: Prune to maintain a manageable canopy and protect ripening crops from birds.

name: Bush Tomato
harvest: Fruit after establishment, timing varies by species and conditions
climate: Arid and semi-arid Australia
tip: Only consume correctly identified edible bush-tomato species and properly ripe fruit; some Solanum species or unripe fruits can be unsafe.

name: Aniseed Myrtle
harvest: Leaves can be harvested lightly once established
water: Regular while young; moderate when established
climate: Subtropical eastern Australia; protected warm-temperate sites
tip: Tip-prune regularly to produce fresh aromatic leaves and maintain a compact plant.

name: Pepperberry
depth: Seed 5–10 mm; plants at nursery level
harvest: Leaves once established; berries on mature female plants after pollination
climate: Cool temperate southeastern Australia
tip: For berries, grow female plants with a compatible male nearby; protect from hot dry exposure.

name: Native Thyme
sun: Part shade to sun depending on species
climate: Temperate to subtropical Australian conditions depending on species
tip: Tip-prune rather than removing large amounts at once to maintain dense growth.

name: Native Basil
propagation: Cuttings or seed depending on species
depth: Seed about 3–5 mm; plants at nursery level
climate: Warm temperate to subtropical depending on species
tip: Regular tip harvesting encourages branching and fresh aromatic foliage.

name: Native Lemongrass
depth: Seed 3–5 mm; divisions at previous soil level
harvest: Leaves can be cut once clumps are established
climate: Warm temperate, subtropical and tropical Australia depending on species
tip: Cut older leaves near the base and allow the centre of the clump to keep producing fresh growth.
